newsitem.title: USA: Bond investors wary on Hilton bid for ITT.
newsitem.headline: Bond investors wary on Hilton bid for ITT.

text.p: Bondholders are wary of the negative credit implications of Hilton Hotels Corp's $10.5 billion bid for ITT Corp, but most are awaiting further developments before taking action, traders said Tuesday.
Spreads on ITT and Hilton bonds widened by 10-20 basis points following news of the Hilton bid, reflecting fears that rating agencies will downgrade the debt of both companies, traders said.
But very few bonds have actually changed hands because many investors believe Hilton's offer will be revised, they said.
"There will definitely be some forced sellers if either company gets downgraded to junk status," said one trader.
At present, both companies have low investment-grade ratings.
Moody's Investors Service Inc rates both Hilton and ITT debt Baa1 is reviewing the ratings for a possible downgrade.
Standard & Poor's Corp rates Hilton BBB-plus and ITT BBB, and has both ratings on CreditWatch with negative implications.
S&P said the cash portion of Hilton's bid, and Hilton's assumption of ITT's $4.2 billion in debt, would increase risk to Hilton debt holders.

The agency added, "However, based on current terms and preliminary analysis of Hilton's financial and operational strategy regarding the acquisiton, S&P expects Hilton to be able to maintain an investment-grade rating."
S&P analyst John Maxwell added, "Our initial sense is that the deal will not be done at current terms and it may cost (Hilton) more."
He added, "The bigger risk is to ITT's rating if the company were to take a takeover defense action."

Frances Schulman, a Moody's analyst, said, "We have placed the companies under review for a possible downgrade because the additional leverage is significant. But we have to see what the final financial structure will look like."
She added, "A downgrade is not a foregone conclusion. We have just indicated it is a possibility."
Traders said ITT's 7-3/8 percent bonds of '15 widened to 125 basis points from 110 basis point over Treasuries Tuesday morning.
Hilton's 7.70 percent notes of '02 widened to 80 basis points from 70 basis points over Treasuries, they said.
Traders said Hilton debt is held mostly by long-term investors and is rarely traded in the market.
